title: Convergent Recommendation Executor: Safety API + Replayable Webhook Protocol for Reversible Batching/Caching Changes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context:
We need a safe, observable API surface and webhook replay semantics for applying, previewing, and rolling back automatic batching/caching recommendations from Optimize. Current prototype clients apply changes via ad-hoc scripts which leads to failures, partial applies, and hard-to-reconcile states. This ticket implements a convergent executor API and a replayable webhook handshake that guarantees either a complete, idempotent application of a recommendation or a well-defined rollback path.

Goals:
- Provide a single Apply API that is idempotent, transactional at the logical recommendation level, and returns a stable operation id for follow-up (status, cancel, rollback).
- Support a Preview API that renders the diff and estimated cost savings without side effects.
- Introduce webhook events for apply lifecycle (requested, accepted, applied, failed, rolled_back) with replayable semantics and an explicit ack layer so retries and out-of-order deliveries are safe.
- Define clear rollback semantics and a safety fence to avoid cascading regressions (e.g., do not auto-rollback a user-modified config without verification).
- Instrument metrics and traces to measure failures, median apply latency, success rate, and cost delta after rollout.

Non-goals:
- Implementing any UI in Console (PM/Design will own that follow-up).
- Rewriting existing optimizer recommendation heuristics (this is integration and reliability work).

Approach summary:
1) API: Add endpoints under /v1/optimizer/exec: POST /apply, POST /preview, GET /operation/{op_id}, POST /operation/{op_id}/rollback, and POST /operation/{op_id}/cancel.
2) Idempotency: Require Idempotency-Key header. Server persists idempotency record keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key) with TTL=30d. POST /apply returns operation_id; subsequent identical requests return same operation_id and status.
3) Two-phase handshake for webhooks: when apply reaches "queued for customer agent", send event "apply.requested" with operation_id and pre-signed verify token. Agent replies with 200/ACK and their agent_signature header. If no ACK after 60s, operation stays queued and retries to alternate route (console or email).
4) Storage: Persist operations and snapshot of all modified configs (JSON blob) so rollback can reconstruct prior state. For large clusters, store diffs and reference keys to configs in object store.
5) Rollback: Rollback is a first-class operation with its own idempotency key. If a rollback fails, mark operation as "rollback_failed" and surface to oncall. Automatic rollback will only be attempted when we can verify the current config matches the snapshot we expect (to avoid rolling back someone else's intentional change).

Implementation details:
- Data model: Operation {operation_id, recommendation_id, customer_id, status, created_at, updated_at, idempotency_key, snapshot_ref, proposed_changes, initiated_by}. Stored in Postgres. Snapshots stored in S3 with version_id.
- Transactionality: Use a compare-and-swap (CAS) pattern for config apply on the agent side; server returns the expected base_config_hash which agent must include when performing apply. If hashes diverge, apply fails fast with conflict code 409.
- API error model: 409 for conflict, 422 for invalid recommendation, 429 for rate-limit, 5xx for transient server errors.
- Security: All endpoints require signed service-to-service JWTs. Webhooks include HMAC signature and a one-time pre-signed verify token for handshake.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preview returns deterministic diff + estimated cost delta without modifying state.
- Apply with same (customer_id, idempotency_key) returns the same operation_id and eventual terminal state.
- Webhook ack handshake tolerates duplicates and out-of-order delivery (tests simulate at-least-once delivery).
- Rollback restores snapshot state when current state matches the snapshot base hash; otherwise returns 409 and requires manual review.
- Metrics and traces generated for 100% of operations.
- Automated E2E test that simulates agent crash/partial-apply and demonstrates safe rollback path.
webhook_handshake:
Event model (apply.requested, apply.accepted, apply.applied, apply.failed, rollback.requested, rollback.completed).
- Delivery: At-least-once via broker, retries exponential backoff.
- Handshake: apply.requested includes verify_token (one-time). Agent must POST /v1/optimizer/agent/ack with {operation_id, verify_token} and include Agent-Signature header. Server marks event acknowledged and proceeds. If ack missing after 60s, server retries delivery and optionally escalates.
- Replay semantics: Webhook includes event_sequence_id and operation_id. Accept duplicates by checking event_sequence_id in persistent store; ignore if already processed.
- Security: each webhook has X-Hub-Signature (HMAC-SHA256) and supporting JWT for agent identity.
idempotency_semantics:
- Idempotency-Key scope: (customer_id, idempotency_key). Keys are opaque client-generated UUIDs.
- Server stores mapping -> operation_id for 30d and returns same operation_id for identical requests.
- Apply is treated as eventual but the operation record is authoritative; clients should poll operation status.
- Rollback gets its own Idempotency-Key and operation record.
- If an operation is in terminal state (applied, rolled_back, failed), replays do not change state and return the terminal record.
- Conflicts when base_config_hash mismatches return 409 and include current_config_hash and suggested resolution steps.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store and TTL behavior. Integration tests: simulated agent that accepts ack, then fails during apply -> ensure rollback path works. Chaos test: simulate duplicated webhooks and out-of-order delivery and validate single-apply invariant. Load test: 500 concurrent apply requests for different customers and 50 repeated idempotent retries. E2E: staging run with 2 internal customers over a week.\n\nSee tests folder: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-tests/tree/eng-61234
rollout_plan:
Alpha (internal): feature_flag=optimizer.exec.alpha enabled for internal customers. Validate metrics and runbook.
Beta: opt-in via org-level flag; allocate support engineer on rotation. Monitor conflicts metric and rollback rate.
GA: flip default ON for small customers first, then expand to enterprise after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Publish API docs and runbook.

Fallback: If 5xx rate > 1% or rollback rate > 3% for 24h, disable auto-apply and route requests to manual review queue.
